review.description: Direct API v2 feedback/current-read contracts gain operation and projection states while stable pages, instances and endpoints retain their structure. Local connection/package guide panels have no new behavior or coverage claim. Existing accessibility and installed-host gaps remain explicit.
review.implementation: Review distinguishes changed widget/connection behavior from containing and transitively affected contracts. Shared bridge, wrapper, operation and snapshot readers implement the changed boundaries; no glossary-to-consumer backlinks or new entity/instance IDs are introduced; new assertion IDs extend actual coverage. Initial feedback and scoped busy state are committed before bridge entry. Snapshot dependency expansion failures retain the pinned original dependency revision, and repaired relationships invalidate the error. Related dependency endpoints are decoded independently; successful generic relationship CAS invalidates old/new endpoints in the same committed revision.
review.tests: New mapped API-V2 assertions cover immediate feedback, current revisions, exact chunks, journal safety, restart recovery and question pages. Existing real assertions are retained without claiming fixture results close native/assistive-technology/soak gaps. API-V2-CURRENT now observes the actual read-ack bridge-entry DOM after a held current-detail response; API-V2-FEEDBACK observes Submitting DOM at actual mutation bridge entry and failed before flushSync. API-V2-DEPENDENCY-ERROR exercises real malformed relationship reads and repair for selected item/conversation projections. Warm malformed-source and malformed-target cases expose real decoding errors through item/conversation reads instead of stale ready; CAS insertion/movement changes their prepared detail versions. Store CAS predicate rejection leaves all endpoint revisions unchanged.

ui:C-ANSWER.implementation: C-ANSWER retains its stable identity and declared implementation anchors. ui:C-STATE-REFRESH.description: C-STATE-REFRESH: Read saved state without a model call. The recorded operation/projection states describe the changed feedback and freshness boundary.
ui:C-STATE-REFRESH.implementation: C-STATE-REFRESH retains its stable identity and declared implementation anchors. The API v2 bridge and worker routing implement acceptance/completion separation; immutable current reads and exact document chunks prepare data in the background. The wrapper scopes busy actions and pending content. The archive receives daemon generation and includes it in accepted-page ownership, reloads the same query after replacement and hides prior selection while pending. Registered selector schemas and explicit1024UTF-8-byte validation precede retained projection admission. Accepted identity and full source/chunk content stay exact. Snapshot original dependency revisions are assigned before relationship expansion errors can return. Endpoint tracking preserves valid peer identities on malformed records and instruments successful CAS using exact old/new bytes. First observed daemon adoption advances the generation before returning; delayed reads from the initial unknown generation retry without changing the accepted daemon.
ui:C-STATE-REFRESH.tests: C-STATE-REFRESH: Pending revisions hide the old source, disable Send, poll again and acknowledge the new revision only after matched detail is displayed.; Large Unicode source is reconstructed exactly, old projections cannot claim a newly committed revision, and unrelated transcript output leaves a prepared inbox ready.; Reopening the same saved database creates a distinct daemon identity; lower and equal serials from the prior instance return current saved data, absent namespaces cannot claim unchanged, and the current namespace retains its unchanged optimization.; An open view accepts lower and equal counters after the daemon identity changes, displays the new source, acknowledges only its new-instance revision, preserves the message draft and returns to the saved inbox without submitting chat.; A held old-instance detail resolves only after current new-instance detail is displayed; actual bridge completion cannot replace or acknowledge old content, and the following action still uses the new identity.; A loaded selected archive page observes replacement without manual refresh; its pending replacement hides the prior page/selection, then displays the new daemon records while preserving archive kind/page-size and usable navigation. Viewing causes no chat submission.; Authenticated read selectors reject1,025 ASCII bytes and1,026 UTF-8 bytes before any projection/operation entry, accept the exact1,024-byte boundary, and reconstruct the entire large source unchanged. Existing explicit gaps remain open; assertion ownership is preserved and no inventory-only test is counted as independent behavior coverage. API-V2-ARCHIVE-INSTANCE exercises completed archive selection, changed daemon envelope, pending new page, preserved nondefaultkind/page-size and no chat; it was observed failing before implementation and passing after it. API-V2-READ-ID rejects over-boundASCII/Unicode requests before any cache/operation entry and verifies exact boundary identities with full large source reconstruction; near-limit rejection timing is measured separately by the isolated API gate. A held current detail blocks all v2 read acknowledgments; after release, exactly one v2 read-ack entry snapshot contains the new displayed source and excludes old source. API-V2-DEPENDENCY-ERROR sends malformed relationships through real item/conversation HTTP reads, requires failed with nonzero saved revision, and checks recovery after a valid saved replacement. API-V2-DEPENDENCY-ERROR now includes warm malformed source/target after useful preparation, and API-V2-RELATIONSHIP-CAS covers warm selected insertion and endpoint movement; the store test checks rejection and unrelated revision isolation. API-V2-FIRST-INSTANCE verifies a delayed initial old reply cannot notify replacement to the old owner after initial-new is accepted; the subsequent unread action uses only initial-new.

ui:S-FACTORY.description: S-FACTORY: Seven navigation tabs and one selected item conversation. Opening does not authorize work. The recorded operation/projection states describe the changed feedback and freshness boundary.
ui:S-FACTORY.implementation: S-FACTORY retains its stable identity and declared implementation anchors. The API v2 bridge and worker routing implement acceptance/completion separation; immutable current reads and exact document chunks prepare data in the background. The wrapper scopes busy actions and pending content. The archive receives daemon generation and includes it in accepted-page ownership, reloads the same query after replacement and hides prior selection while pending. Background log jobs reserve captured-buffer capacity across all handlers and omit replay bodies/headers/context, leaving redaction/write outside dispatch. Registered selector schemas and explicit1024UTF-8-byte validation precede retained projection admission. Accepted identity and full source/chunk content stay exact. Queue removal zeroes obsolete callback slots. Status and duplicate submission share current document-availability normalization, leaving identity/state authoritative and never replaying work. Initial feedback and scoped disabled actions are committed with flushSync before invoking the bridge. First observed daemon adoption advances the generation before returning; delayed reads from the initial unknown generation retry without changing the accepted daemon.
ui:S-FACTORY.tests: S-FACTORY: Local Submitting feedback precedes a held bridge in less than 100 ms; queued/running work keeps its draft and scope disabled while navigation remains usable; only success clears the draft.; Persisted running effects recover as uncertain, missing old-instance work reports lost, and neither identity is resubmitted.; Reopening the same saved database creates a distinct daemon identity; lower and equal serials from the prior instance return current saved data, absent namespaces cannot claim unchanged, and the current namespace retains its unchanged optimization.; An open view accepts lower and equal counters after the daemon identity changes, displays the new source, acknowledges only its new-instance revision, preserves the message draft and returns to the saved inbox without submitting chat.; A held old-instance detail resolves only after current new-instance detail is displayed; actual bridge completion cannot replace or acknowledge old content, and the following action still uses the new identity.; Navigation and the saved draft survive a held command across daemon replacement; its late response is reconciled by the original instance/request pair as uncertain, with explicit inspection guidance and exactly one submission.; A loaded selected archive page observes replacement without manual refresh; its pending replacement hides the prior page/selection, then displays the new daemon records while preserving archive kind/page-size and usable navigation. Viewing causes no chat submission.; Two authenticated handlers share byte admission for64near-limit completed RPCs behind a held sink. Retained heap stays below32MiB over baseline and accounted body/response/URL buffers stay within8MiB; later same-handler records report byte-pressure drops without writing raw command text.; Authenticated read selectors reject1,025 ASCII bytes and1,026 UTF-8 bytes before any projection/operation entry, accept the exact1,024-byte boundary, and reconstruct the entire large source unchanged.; Decreasing bursts of 8, 5 and 3 payload-capturing operations execute once, drain all live byte/scope accounting and leave every obsolete pending backing slot zero, releasing completed input closures.; Actual document-cache eviction removes terminal success/error chunks; authenticated duplicate submissions preserve original identity/tool/state, explicitly report unavailable details with no dead descriptors, and execute no additional work. Existing explicit gaps remain open; assertion ownership is preserved and no inventory-only test is counted as independent behavior coverage. API-V2-ARCHIVE-INSTANCE exercises completed archive selection, changed daemon envelope, pending new page, preserved nondefaultkind/page-size and no chat; it was observed failing before implementation and passing after it. API-V2-LOG-BYTES uses two authenticated handlers,64near-limit bodies and a held sink; post-GC heap/accounted-byte bounds and subsequent drop/no-payload records are asserted. This supplies actual shared-boundary coverage, not a new visual widget promise. API-V2-READ-ID rejects over-boundASCII/Unicode requests before any cache/operation entry and verifies exact boundary identities with full large source reconstruction; near-limit rejection timing is measured separately by the isolated API gate. API-V2-INPUT-RELEASE inspects the actual backing array after decreasing drained bursts with exact effects/accounting. API-V2-DUPLICATE-DETAIL evicts actual chunk documents and tests authenticated original duplicate identities for unavailable flags/no descriptors/no replay. The synchronous bridge-entry snapshot now requires Submitting DOM before session_chat invocation; it failed before the commit change and passes afterward while preserving all draft/navigation/delivery assertions. API-V2-FIRST-INSTANCE verifies a delayed initial old reply cannot notify replacement to the old owner after initial-new is accepted; the subsequent unread action uses only initial-new.
